entries.snippet: J4 treatment was given ad libitum in the drinking water at the concentration of 0.06 mg/ml. J4 was dissolved in the drinking water containing 1% HPβCD, which served as the vehicle. The total treatment time was 10 weeks. The average daily intake for a laboratory mouse was estimated to be 0.17 ml/g/day [49]. Thus, the dose of 0.06 mg/ml J4 in drinking water would approximately give an overall dose of 10.2 mg/kg/day for the mice in this study.

entries.proposition: Among the limitations the authors list: the mechanism linking mTOR-pathway effects to myelination is unclear, lineage progression from OPCs to mature oligodendrocytes is not directly shown, and adenosine was not directly measured with its downstream receptor pathways undefined. Males only and the mild model are discussed elsewhere in the paragraph and are not claimed here.
entries.snippet: Third, while our data suggest that J4 may indirectly modulate mTOR signaling and dampen neuronal hyperactivity, the precise mechanistic relationship between these pathways and myelination remains unclear and warrants further investigation. Fourth, our findings are consistent with enhanced oligodendroglial maturation in WM regions following J4 treatment, yet the current data do not directly demonstrate lineage progression from OPCs to mature oligodendrocytes. Finally, although J4 is known to elevate extracellular adenosine levels through ENT1 inhibition, the direct measurement of adenosine and the downstream molecular pathways through which adenosine receptor signaling influences oligodendroglial maturation are not yet fully defined in this present study and require further investigation.

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Quote widened to the third, fourth and final limitations; proposition reduced to those three.

entries.proposition: Normal-brain treated arm: WT mice receiving J4 are compared with WT Veh for myelin thickness against axon diameter. Three facts on three surfaces: (1) the text first prints F(1, 974) = 1.986, p = 0.1591 for the WT Veh versus WT J4 g-ratio slope comparison (Fig 4C, and the sentence says no significant change); (2) a few sentences later it prints the same F(1, 974) = 1.986 with p = 0.0158 for the myelin-thickness comparison and calls it a slight increase (Fig 4D); (3) the Fig 4D middle panel (WT Veh versus WT J4, N = 3 each) carries a single-star bracket, i.e. the figure signals significance at the 0.05 level, and the Fig 4C middle panel carries 'ns'. F(1, 974) = 1.986 corresponds to p of about 0.16 (my recomputation, matched by the auditor), so the printed p = 0.0158 does not fit that F: it is a defect in the text (a mis-typed F or p), but the star means the source does signal significance for this comparison and which printed value is wrong cannot be settled from the paper alone. OFT and NOR show no change in WT J4 (Fig 1). Whether this is the only measure of J4 in a non-mutant brain was not established (Figs 5 and 6 not fully read).
entries.snippet: while WT J4 group showed a slight increase of myelin thickness when compared to WT Veh controls (F(1, 974) = 1.986, p = 0.0158)
